system.name: Local redundancy
system.one_liner: An information-theoretic plasticity measure: worst-case redundancy of a local model family, lower-bounded by the expected squared gradient norm on a synthetic memorization task.

content.variant_note: three lettered panels in a row, each carrying one claim: geometric intuition, lower-bound sketch with its inequality, result bar chart
content.argues: Plasticity can be measured as the information radius of the local model family; a gradient-norm bound makes it computable and predicts downstream performance better than common heuristics.
content.subject: High and low plasticity as information circles, a blob sketch of the lower bound with its inequality, and a bar chart of metrics.

lessons.what_to_learn: Express an abstract quantity as a radius: draw a large and a small circle with the same centre marker for high versus low capacity, then sketch the bound as a short step arrow inside a longer dashed radius with the inequality in a box below.
lessons.suits: Theory-driven papers that introduce a new measure with an intuition, a bound and one empirical comparison, each fitting a small panel.

evidence: a plastic network can reach many distributions (large radius); a rigid network cannot (small radius)
The expected squared gradient norm on synthetic memorization data lower-bounds local redundancy (Theorem 3.4)
Local redundancy: a principled, computable measure of plasticity.

summary: The paper introduces local redundancy, an information-theoretic measure of a network's plasticity derived from universal compression theory, and shows that the expected squared gradient norm on a synthetic memorization task lower-bounds it. Figure 1 is a three-panel hero figure in serif matplotlib style. Panel (a) draws plasticity as information radius: a large blue circle (high plasticity) beside a small red circle (low plasticity), each with a centre point and a radius arrow. Panel (b) sketches the local model family as a grey blob with a short gradient step and a longer brown dashed radius, with the inequality in a pale-yellow box. Panel (c) is a bar chart in which local redundancy (blue) predicts future task performance better than four grey baseline metrics.
summary_zh: 论文提出可塑性度量“局部冗余”，并证明其下界是合成记忆任务上的期望梯度范数平方。图 1 为三联图：(a) 大蓝圈与小红圈表示高低可塑性；(b) 灰色斑块、梯度步与虚线半径配合不等式展示下界；(c) 柱状图显示它比四个基线更能预测后续表现。
notes: Prior labels kept in order (contribution-mosaic, concept-schematic). The three panels also read as a narrative (principled, computable, predictive) but no process arrows run between them. The formula is read from the digest text; error bars in (c) have no stated meaning.
